Musical theatre’s graveyard is littered with grand scale projects at which producers threw their millions and ended up with a flop. Thankfully the opposite is also true, where an unlikely premise, when infused with heart, enthusiasm, talent and energy, can result in a surprising and uplifting success.
Why Am I So Single? is warm, bold and overflowing with ideas.
Good as all these songs are, there are too many here – although I'd be sad to lose bonkers tangents like the operatic panic over a bee.
Why Am I So Single? feels somewhat flabby.
In many ways, this might be exactly the show a too often overly cautious West End needs right now and the energy in the house was good evidence for that conclusion.
When you're playing a hallowed venue like the Garrick, people expect a bit more polish.
"Why Am I So Single?" has arrived in the West End with no tryout in which its major structural problems could have been addressed.
I defy anyone not to have a massively enjoyable time at this musical.
...is a very fun watch, with bop after bop.

It's a phenomenally powerful rug-pull, in a show that presents itself as a frothy look at how modern is dating is awful, to include one of the most emotionally devastating musical theatre numbers of recent times.
Ultimately, Why Am I So Single? can't quite get beyond the fact a very thin book stops the show dead between the musical numbers, despite everyone's best efforts.

Unfortunately, it is not quite there yet. The self-referencing nature of the show includes the immortal line 'Have you seen the state of the West End lately? They'll put on any old sh**'. While I wouldn't quite go that far, Why Am I So Single? is far too messy in its current state.
This is fun, there's no denying that, but it does feel long at just over 2 1/2 hours.

cn.t: The Six creators deliver a meta, self-indulgent musical about modern dating that's catchy and fun but lacks the laser-sharp focus of their debut. Critics are split: some find it inventive and heartfelt, others say it sags under expectations.
